title: Weesuck
summary: Weesuck is the clearer modern form of the longer placename Achabachawesuck. It refers to a small creek or brook between Fourth Neck and Pine Neck in what was historically Atlanticville, now the East Quogue area of Southampton.
introduction_content: Weesuck Creek preserves a Native place name within the East Quogue shoreline. The longer recorded form, Achabachawesuck, identifies a creek between Fourth Neck and Pine Neck, in the community later called Atlanticville. Tooker, pp. 3–4, 281–282
history_content: Seventeenth- and eighteenth-century boundary descriptions used this creek together with paths, necks and meadows to locate land. Those records preserve fragments of a named Indigenous landscape even as colonial surveyors divided it into holdings. Weesuck is a shortened recorded form, not evidence that the older community’s geography began with those surveys. Tooker, pp. 3–4, 281–282
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Achabachawesuck, Achabachwesuck, Achabusuckwesuck, Achabuchawesuck, Wesuck, and Weesuck. Tooker interprets the full form as a separated or turning-aside little brook, in practical terms a boundary brook.

Why Place Names Matter

“Historically, a study of the names of places and topographical features can reveal much about how people viewed and related with the land.”

— Nna O. Uluocha, Decolonizing place-names: Strategic imperative for preserving indigenous cartography in post-colonial Africa (2015), full text, discussion of place-names and environmental knowledge
whereintheworld_content:
Weesuck Creek lies at East Quogue, between Fourth Neck and Pine Neck, and opens southward into Shinnecock Bay. Tooker places the longer name Achabachawesuck between these two necks in the locality then called Atlanticville. Tooker (1911), pp. 3–4, 281–282.

The dot and shaded area identify the present creek and its inner shoreline. They do not mark the separate Phillips Creek or Daves Creek farther southwest.
